Question B-007-008-005.

Why the correct answer is right: Scatter is inefficient. Most transmitted energy follows the main path or is lost, and only a small fraction is redirected toward receivers in the skip zone, so the received signal is weak.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Propagation through ground waves absorbs most of the signal energy": Ground-wave loss is not the cause of a weak high frequency (HF) scatter signal arriving from the skip zone.
- sourceIndex 2: "The F region of the ionosphere absorbs most of the signal energy": The F region is mainly the refracting region for many HF paths. Heavy absorption is more associated with lower regions.
- sourceIndex 3: "Auroral activity absorbs most of the signal energy": Auroral absorption or distortion can happen in special conditions, but ordinary HF scatter weakness comes from very little energy being redirected to the receiver.
